title: Lionel Hampton and Bunny Berigan in the Goodman band
summary: Gil calls Hampton a hard leader but a beautiful vibraphonist, praises Berigan's exciting trumpet and his alcoholism, and recalls the Tommy Dorsey hit records.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Lionel Hampton is really what is known affectionately in the trade as a motherfucker. (LAUGHTER). He's known mostly, you know, you've heard people talk about him as the band leader that

pockets all the money and doesn't pay anybody. And he's a millionaire and he's a capitalist and all that. Which is all true, but the thing about him is that he's a beautiful musician. He's a swinger and he can play those vibes...wow!....

I heard him on TV in Paris a couple of years ago and it reminded me all of a sudden how great he is, you know. So Lionel was with Benny Goodman, so was Teddy Wilson and a trumpet player, a white trumpet player named, Bunny Berigan in. A very exciting trumpet player.
He made that one big record.

And when he played you know, you knew something was going to happen. He was a trapeze man. Sometimes he fell on his face and he didn't care. But most of the time he played. He could play. He was a terrible alcoholic and was determined to kill himself which he did, drinking.
'I can't get started with you'. A big record, yes.
He made some beautiful ones also like, of course luckily so, not one of the lots of his solos are not well recorded or they're on radio station tapes; somebody probably has them by now.

Everybody has them by now. But he made a couple of Tommy Dorsey records, 'Who' and 'Marie'. 'Marie' and 'Song of India' those are the two. That was back to back on a record and those two sales were sensational.
It's hard to really explain that to people because you had to hear him in person to get it.
